text: [Lab.C. §§ 3755, 3757] [3:518 - 3:524] Reserved. 2. [3:525] Coverage for Intentional Injury: Because workers' compensation insurance covers the employer's liability in such proceedings, even intentional acts by the insured employer are covered. The Workers' Compensation Act provides the exclusive remedy for work-related injuries “notwithstanding that the injury resulted from the intentional conduct of the employer, and even though the employer's conduct might be characterized as egregious.” [Shoemaker v. Myers, supra, 52 C3d at 18, 276 CR at 314] a. [3:526] Ins.C. § 533 not applicable: Therefore, the Ins.C. § 533 bar on coverage for liability arising from the insured's “wilful acts” (see ¶ 3:105 ff.) does not apply to workers' compensation insurance. [Azevedo v. Abel (1968) 264 CA2d 451, 458, 70 CR 710, 714] b. [3:527] Limitation—no coverage for “serious and willful misconduct” penalty: Workers' compensation awards may 2 be increased by 50% where “serious and willful misconduct” by the “employer” is shown. But the workers' compensation insurer may not indemnify the employer against this penalty (see ¶ 3:549). [3:528 - 3:534] Reserved. 3.
